findings.title: S3 bucket policy does not enforce TLS (SecureTransport)
findings.description: Without an explicit Deny on aws:SecureTransport=false, bucket objects can be fetched over plaintext HTTP. Add a bucket policy statement denying s3:* when SecureTransport is false.
findings.expected: bucket policy denying s3:* when SecureTransport is false
findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

findings.title: S3 bucket without server access logging
findings.description: Server access logging records requests against the bucket, which is essential for audit and incident response.
findings.remediation: Enable audit logging. Turn on CloudTrail (multi-region, log file validation, KMS-encrypted bucket), VPC flow logs, and service access logs. Ship logs to a dedicated, MFA-delete-protected bucket in a security account.

findings.title: S3 bucket without lifecycle configuration
findings.description: Hygiene: S3 buckets should define lifecycle rules to transition or expire objects, controlling long-term storage costs. Add a lifecycle_rule block or an aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration resource.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: S3 bucket encrypted with AWS-managed key, no customer-managed key
findings.description: This bucket encrypts objects with an AWS-managed key (SSE-S3 AES256, or SSE-KMS with the AWS-managed aws/s3 key) instead of a customer-managed KMS key. A CMK gives you key rotation control, grants, CloudTrail audit of key use, and the ability to disable or delete the key. Set kms_master_key_id to a customer-managed key. Unencrypted buckets are AEGIS-AWS-001's job and are not reported here.
findings.expected: kms_master_key_id set to a customer-managed KMS key
findings.remediation: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

findings.title: GKE cluster without network policy
findings.description: google_container_cluster with no network_policy block, or with network_policy disabled, allows unrestricted pod-to-pod traffic.
findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace broad roles with the minimum predefined or custom IAM roles the workload needs. Use Workload Identity Federation and service accounts with minimal scopes.

findings.title: GKE cluster not private
findings.description: google_container_cluster with no private_cluster_config block assigns public IPs to nodes. Use private clusters so nodes have internal IPs only.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Google Cloud security best practices and the CIS Google Cloud Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.evidence: workload_identity_config = absent (metadata server v2 not enforced)
findings.expected: workload_identity_config { workload_pool = "...svc.id.goog" } or node_config { workload_metadata_config { mode = "GKE_METADATA" } }

findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace broad roles with the minimum predefined or custom IAM roles the workload needs. Use Workload Identity Federation and service accounts with minimal scopes.

findings.title: GKE control plane publicly reachable
findings.description: google_container_cluster with no private endpoint and master_authorized_networks_config absent or allowing 0.0.0.0/0 exposes the Kubernetes API to the internet.
findings.expected: private_cluster_config { enable_private_endpoint = true } or master_authorized_networks_config with restricted cidr_blocks
findings.remediation: Remove public exposure. Restrict ingress to known CIDR ranges, disable public IPs / public access, and use Private Service Connect / VPC Service Controls if external access is required. Verify with `gcloud compute firewall-rules list`.

findings.title: GKE cluster without a release channel

findings.title: GKE cluster without security posture management
findings.description: google_container_cluster with no security_posture_config block (or vulnerability_mode = "DISABLED") gets no workload vulnerability scanning: known CVEs in running workloads go unreported. Enable security posture management.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Google Cloud security best practices and the CIS Google Cloud Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: GKE cluster nodes with legacy metadata endpoints enabled
findings.description: google_container_cluster node_config.metadata without disable-legacy-endpoints = "true" exposes the legacy GCE metadata endpoints (v0.1/v1beta1) on nodes, widening SSRF and credential-theft impact. Disable legacy endpoints.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Google Cloud security best practices and the CIS Google Cloud Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: GKE cluster without application-layer secrets encryption
findings.description: google_container_cluster with no database_encryption block stores Kubernetes secrets in etcd encrypted only at the storage layer with Google-managed keys. Enable application-layer secrets encryption with a customer-managed Cloud KMS key.
findings.remediation: Enable encryption at rest. Google-managed keys apply by default; for regulated data use customer-managed keys (CMEK) via Cloud KMS with key rotation.

findings.title: GKE cluster without Google Groups for RBAC
findings.description: google_container_cluster with no authenticator_groups_config block cannot bind Kubernetes RBAC to Google Groups: access is managed per-user instead of through group membership, which drifts during onboarding and offboarding. Configure authenticator_groups_config.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Google Cloud security best practices and the CIS Google Cloud Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: GKE cluster without VPC-native networking
findings.description: google_container_cluster with no ip_allocation_policy block uses routes-based networking, which lacks alias IPs for pods: network policies and VPC flow logs cannot distinguish pod traffic. Use VPC-native clusters with ip_allocation_policy.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Google Cloud security best practices and the CIS Google Cloud Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: GKE node boot disks without customer-managed encryption
findings.description: google_container_cluster / google_container_node_pool node_config without boot_disk_kms_key encrypts node boot disks with Google-managed keys only. Assign a customer-managed Cloud KMS key for control over rotation and revocation.
findings.remediation: Enable encryption at rest. Google-managed keys apply by default; for regulated data use customer-managed keys (CMEK) via Cloud KMS with key rotation.
